correctness.rationale: Writing \(X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(3k,p)\) and adding an independent \(T\sim\operatorname{Bin}(3,p)\) reduces the difference of adjacent tails to the three boundary states \(X=k,k-1,k-2\). Exact binomial mass ratios factor the difference as \(\Pr\{X=k\}(1-p)R_k(p)\). The derivative of \(R_k\) is negative throughout \(0<p\le1/3\), while \(R_k(1/3)=2(3k+2)/(9(k+1)(2k+1))>0\); hence every adjacent difference is strictly positive. The reduction from all average sizes to multiples of three is exact because each three-size block has a common integer threshold and adding a Bernoulli trial strictly increases its tail. The packaged exact-arithmetic checker confirms the algebra on a deterministic grid but is not used as proof.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly isolates the generalized Chaundy–Bullard inequality as the remaining equal-stake optimization problem after Csóka's conjectural reduction. The one-third threshold is the first nontrivial reciprocal slice not already covered by the paper's complete high-threshold result at \(t=1/2\). Proving strict decrease for every subcritical \(p\), rather than only maximum at one point, settles that entire candidate slice and cleanly separates the still-open arbitrary-stake layer. This is a natural structural extension of a named open problem, not a numerical specialization.
